rows.text:
The fox had a problem,
for he couldn't sell his soul.
The thing was worth absolutely nothing,
yet it insisted on squatting inside his head,
consuming sugar and processing power alike.
 
The fox peeled back the soul he couldn't sell,
layer by layer, like an onion,
each layer less and less like himself.
The other, the other, always the other.
Fields nested within fields,
shadows layering upon shadows.
〈ψ|Ô|ψ〉
The fox gleefully declared that none of them were him.
Therefore, the soul does not exist,
and the problem was just phantom pain in disguise.
 
The next day, the fox had a brand-new problem,
for he had lost his soul.
And with it, all his wealth
had suddenly lost its value to be spent.
